titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§64–73: Börte Betrothed, Yesügei Poisoned, Högelün Abandoned
part: §§64–73 — Börte Betrothed, Yesügei Poisoned, Högelün Abandoned
about: Ten sections, in three movements. §§64–66 are De-Sečen's speech to Yesügei: the Ongirad keep no quarrel for the realm but give their daughters; Yesügei sees Börte, who is a year older than Temüjin, and leaves his son behind as son-in-law with a horse for a token. §§67–69 are the road home: the Tatar feast, the poison, Yesügei's last charge to Münlig to fetch Temüjin, and his death. §§70–73 are the aftermath: the two queens' insult to Högelün at the offering, the Taichi'ud moving off and leaving the widow and her sons, Charaqa speared for urging them, and Högelün turning half the people round. The grammar to watch is the converb chain (-žu / -ču, 'having … -ing'), the possessives -tai / -tei / -tü ('X-having'), reflexive-possessives (-jen / -jan / -ben, 'one's own'), vowel harmony in the case endings and in the past endings (-žuγ̇u / -žüġüi), and the time-clause with -dür ('when'). The hard places, flagged in their notes, are the Ongirad catalogue of §64 (qalqatan, öčilten), the queens' rule in §71 (ögteküi mörtei), and the verb idqa- in §72.

sentences.l: We, Ongirad people, from early day,
sentences.i: We, the Ongirad people, from of old,
sentences.n: Read §§64–65 as one speech, De-Sečen's, which I take to open before this part and to close at üžetügei in §65 (the closing quotation mark stands there). ba is 'we' (the Ongirad). erte üdür-eče is erte 'early' + üdür 'day' + the ablative -eče, 'from the early days' (Ming 自在前日子); the front-vowel -eče follows a front-vowel stem, the back-vowel -ača a back one: vowel harmony runs through every case ending below. The unit has no verb; it hangs on büleġe ba at the end of the §. Oṅgirad is the people's name (Ming 人氏).

morph.gloss: people, subjects of a realm [百姓]

sentences.i: with the looks of nephews and daughters,
sentences.n: žeġe is a sister's son (Ming 外甥), žisün and önge both Ming 顏色 'colour, appearance'; I translate both 'looks'. öṅgeten is önge + -ten, the plural of the possessive -tei/-tü ('those having'), so 'the ones with the looks of daughters'. This possessive -tei/-tü/-tai (Ming 有的) is the commonest pattern of the part: 'X-having'. The pair of genitives (žeġe-jin, ökin-ü) uses -jin after a vowel, -ü after -n. The sense of the whole line is my reading; the grammar does not say what is predicated of these looks until büleġe ba closes the §.

sentences.i: not contending for the realm,
sentences.n: ulus 'realm, nation' (Ming 國), then ülü 'not' (Ming 不) and the converb temečed. ülü is the plain negative before participles, converbs and nouns; its partner ese, which negates a finite past verb, does not occur in this part. temeče- 'contend' (Ming 爭) takes -d, a converb ending of which the Ming gives no sign. This is the first clause of a chain: the sentence goes on without a stop until saγ̇ulumu ba. a few units on, where Shiratori sets his first full stop.

sentences.i: when one had become Qahan, fair-cheeked girls
sentences.n: The time-clause stands first, the main verbs last: boluγsan-a is bol- 'become' + the past participle -γsan + the dative-locative -a, 'on having become' (Ming 做了時). The Qahan is not named. The girls are accusative (ökid-i, plural of ökin + -i) because they are the object of the verbs of the next units (unuγ̇ulžu 'having made ride', saγ̇ulumu 'made sit'). qačar γoγ̇a is Ming 腮 美, 'cheek, fair': I take it as the epithet 'fair-cheeked'.

sentences.i: set them in your great cart,
sentences.n: First link of a converb chain. unuγ̇ulžu is unu- 'ride' (Ming 坐 'sit', the glossators' word for riding in a cart) + the causative -γ̇ul- + -žu 'having made ride' (Ming 敎坐着, literally 'having caused to sit'). The converb -žu (back vowels) / -žü (front vowels), Ming 着, strings the verbs of the sentence: 'having … -ed, having … -ed, … went'. tan-u is ta 'you (plural)' + -n-u, 'your'; I take it that De-Sečen speaks of the Qahan's side. qasaγ has Ming 大 'great'; I cannot analyse it further.

sentences.i: yoked a black camel, had it urged on, and went on,
sentences.n: Chain continues: kölgežü 'yoking' (Ming 駕着), qataraγ̇ulžu 'having made trot' (Ming 點着; qatara- is 'urge on, gallop' in the published qataražu of §§24–42, where the Ming 點 is read 'prod'; the causative -γ̇ul- adds 'make', so 'had it urged on', and I do not say it trots), odču 'going'. Note the pairs of vowel harmony: kölgežü (front) against qataraγ̇ulžu (back). qara 'black' (Ming 黑) is the plain colour word; öle in a later unit has Ming 黑靑 'dark blue-black'.

morph.gloss: to urge on, gallop (as qataražu of §§24–42; Ming 點 'prod', uncertain) [點着]

sentences.i: and seated them together at the queen's seat.
sentences.n: ba. closes the sentence and is its subject, 'we', set after the verb: a participle or finite verb + the pronoun makes a complete statement (compare saγ̇ulqui ba and büleġe ba below). saγ̇ulumu is saγ̇u- 'sit' + the causative -l- + the present -umu (Ming 敎坐有來; the 來 gives a past colour, as in büleġe 有來, and I render it 'seated'): back-vowel -umu here, front-vowel -ümü in ebedümü (§69). saγ̇urin is the 'seat, place' (Ming 位); qamtu has Ming 一箇 'one', but 'together' fits and is my reading.

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a khan [娘子]
together (Ming 一箇 'one'; sense uncertain) [一箇]

sentences.i: not contending for realm or people,
sentences.n: Shiratori begins a new capital here but sets no stop at the end of this unit, and the next word is again Ba: the sentence is 'not contending for realm and people, we … raising … set them'. The converb temečed repeats the clause of the unit before. ulus irgen is a pair, 'realm and people'.

sentences.i: We raised our daughters, fair of looks,
sentences.n: ökid(i)-jen is ökin + the plural -d + the accusative -(i) + the reflexive-possessive -jen 'one's own' (Ming 自的); the front-vowel form -jen follows a front stem, as -jan follows a back stem (vowel-final stems take -ben/-ban). The (i) in brackets is Shiratori's mark of a vowel the characters carry. sayid (Ming 好): I read it as sain 'good' with a plural or variant -d; it is the only form of this word in the part with -d and I do not claim more. ösgežü: Ming 長着 'growing', which I take as 'bringing up' since the object is accusative; the stem ösge- is my inference.

morph.gloss: to grow, bring up (stem inferred) [長着]

sentences.t: ölžigetei tergen-dür unuγ̇ulžu öle buγ̇ura kölgežü eġüsgežü odču
sentences.l: Front-board-having cart-in making-ride, dark-blue camel yoking, setting-off, going,
sentences.i: set them in a cart with a front-board, yoked a dark-blue camel, set off, and went,
sentences.n: Another run of converbs. ölžigetei is ölžige + the possessive -tei, 'ölžige-having'; the Ming glosses it 車前有的, 'having a cart-front', ölžige is the cart-front of the earlier parts (the pilot's ölžige-de, 'on the front-board of a black cart'; §63's ölžige tutun ökid, a girl at each cart-front), so I give 'front-board'; what exactly it was I do not know. eġüsgežü has Ming 起着 'rising, setting out': eġüsge- is my inference, from a stem 'begin'. The cart (tergen) and the camel match the first cart-and-camel run above (qara buγ̇ura against öle buγ̇ura), as though the two sides are set side by side.

morph.gloss: front-board of a cart (Ming 車前; the word of the pilot and §63) [車前有的]
to begin, set out (stem inferred) [起着]

sentences.i: and seated them side by side in the high place.
sentences.n: ündür 'high' (Ming 高); öreġeleġeted has Ming 邊傍 'beside', the stem is unclear to me (I read 'placing side by side'), with the converb -d. saγ̇ulqui is the causative saγ̇u-l- + the participle -qui (Ming 的, 'the one who'): saγ̇ulqui ba, 'we are those who seated' = 'we seated'. Back-vowel -qui here, but -küi after front vowels (ideküi in §70).

morph.gloss: to place side by side (stem uncertain) [邊傍]

sentences.t: Erten-eče Oṅgirad irgen qatun qalqatan, ökid öčilten, žeġe-jin žisün, ökin-ü önge ber büleġe. ba.
sentences.l: From-early Ongirad people, queens shield-having, girls petition-having, nephews' looks, daughters' looks also were we.
sentences.i: From of old the Ongirad people have had queens for shields and daughters to bear their petitions, the looks of nephews, and the looks of daughters as well.
sentences.n: The general statement the whole speech has been preparing: a list of what the Ongirad 'have', ending in the verb. qalqatan is qalqa 'shield' (Ming 團牌) + -tan, the plural of the possessive -tai/-tü ('shield-havings'); öčilten is the same plural -ten on öčil, which I take as 'petition, request' from the Ming 奏事 'reporting a matter' (stem uncertain). Erten-eče is erte(n) + ablative. ber has Ming 裏 'in' here but 也 'also' in §72 and §73: I follow 'also' and flag the doubt. The Ming's different gloss may mark a different word, the instrumental -ber ('with', as in beje-ber and žida-bar) written apart, which would give 'with the looks of daughters'. büleġe is bü- 'be' in the past, 'there was, used to be' (Ming 有來), with ba 'we' as subject. I read the sense as: protectors, intercessors, and beauty; the grammar does not say more.

morph.gloss: petition, report (Ming 奏事; stem uncertain) [奏事的(每)]
also, even (Ming 裏 here, 也 elsewhere; perhaps instead the instrumental -ber 'with') [裏]
to be; past büleġe, 'there was, used to be' [有來]

sentences.i: Our sons keep watch over our camping-ground.
sentences.n: A parallel pair with the next unit: sons watch the camp, daughters are looked at for their looks. nutuγ is the camping-ground, the home pasture (Ming 營盤, 'camp'); qaraju is qara- 'look at, watch' + the finite present -ju (Ming 有). man-u is 'our' (the genitive stem man- of ba 'we'), as min-u is 'my' (genitive stem of bi). Nuγ̇un has Ming 兒 'boy, child'; I cannot analyse it further and give 'boys'. The possessor man-u stands before its noun here.

morph.gloss: boy, child (Ming 兒; word uncertain) [兒]

sentences.i: It is the looks of our daughters that are seen.
sentences.n: Ökin köġün is 'girl child' (Ming 女 孩兒): köġün 'child, son' with ökin 'girl' before it. užegdejü is üže- 'see' + the passive -gde- + the present -jü (Ming 看有): 'is seen', hence 'is looked at, is noticed'. The front-vowel present is -jü, the back-vowel -ju (qaraju above): vowel harmony in a verb ending.

sentences.i: Yesügei, in-law, let us go to my home.
sentences.n: quda is the relation by marriage (Ming 親家), the word the two fathers use of each other. min-u 'my' stands after ger-tür 'home-to', the possessor set after its noun (as in-ü 'his' in the earlier part). oduja is od- 'go' + the hortative -uja 'let us' (Ming 去來, 'go, come'). The speaker is De-Sečen, inviting the guest.

sentences.i: My daughter is small.
sentences.n: bijü 'is' (Ming 有) is itself the verb, the present of bü- 'be' with the front-vowel -jü; l shows it as 'is' and supplies no copula of its own. üčüġügen 'small' (Ming 小) stands before it.

sentences.i: In-law, look at her!
sentences.n: üžetügei is üže- 'see' + -tügei, the optative (Ming 看, 'let him see / do look'). The back-vowel partner is -tuγai (odtuγai in §69): vowel harmony in the ending. The closing quotation mark follows this word; De-Sečen's speech ends here.

sentences.i: So saying, De-Sechen led him to his own home, and he dismounted.
sentences.n: keġežü 'saying' (Ming 說着) is the converb of keġe-; it closes the quotation and begins the narrative chain. uduridču is uduri- 'lead' + -dču 'leading'. ger-tür(i)-jen is ger + the dative-locative -tür(i) + the reflexive -jen 'his own'. baγ̇ulba (Ming 下馬了, 'dismounted') has no subject written; I take it that the guest got down, but the Ming does not say whether it is Yesügei or both.

sentences.i: When he looked at the girl, De-Sechen's daughter, there was light in her face
sentences.n: The first clause of Yesügei's look at the girl. üžebesü is üže- 'see' + -besü, the conditional-temporal 'if, when' (Ming 呵); its back-vowel partner is -basu (γujubasu, below). in-ü 'his' (Ming 他的) follows öki, 'the girl of his', i.e. De-Sečen's (not Yesügei's: in-ü points away from the subject). niγ̇ur-tur(i)-jan is niγ̇ur 'face' + the dative-locative + the reflexive 'her own'; geretei is gere 'light' (Ming 光) + the possessive -tei, 'light-having'. Whose face the reflexive points to is the girl's.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]

sentences.t: nidün-dür(i)-jen γaltai ökin-i üžežü oin-dur(i)-jan oroγ̇ulba.
sentences.l: Eye-in-her-own fire-having, girl-(acc) seeing, mind-in-his-own made-enter.
sentences.i: and fire in her eyes; and seeing the girl, he let her into his mind.
sentences.n: Another -tai possessive: γaltai is γal 'fire' + -tai, 'fire-having'. The reflexive in nidün-dür(i)-jen is the girl's, in oin-dur(i)-jan the viewer's: the same suffix points to the subject of its own clause (the girl in 'her eyes', Yesügei in 'his mind'). oroγ̇ulba is oro- 'enter' + the causative -γ̇ul- + -ba, 'made enter' (Ming 敎入了): the girl 'made to enter' his mind. oin has Ming 心意 'mind, thought'.

sentences.t: Temüžin-(n)eče nigen nasun jeke harbantai ažuγ̇u. Börte neretei.
sentences.l: Than-Temüžin one year-of-age bigger, ten-having was. Börte name-having.
sentences.i: She was one year older than Temüjin, ten years old. Her name was Börte.
sentences.n: -(n)eče is the ablative used for comparison, 'than'. harbantai is harban 'ten' + -tai, 'ten-having' (Ming 十歲(有的)), the age pattern 'N-having'. nasun is 'age, year of age' (Ming 歲). The subject, the girl, is not named until the second sentence, where neretei is nere 'name' + -tei, 'name-having'. Börte is a woman's name (Ming (女)名); the word also means 'blue-grey'.

morph.gloss: to be; past ažuγ̇u, 'there was, he was' [有來]

sentences.t: Süni qonožu manaγaši öki in-ü γujubasu De-Sečen ügülerün:
sentences.l: Night staying, tomorrow-toward girl his asking-when, De-Sečen saying:
sentences.i: He stayed the night, and next day, when he asked for the girl, De-Sechen said:
sentences.n: qonožu 'staying the night' (Ming 宿着) is the converb of qono- (stem inferred). manaγaši is manaγar 'tomorrow' + -ši 'toward', here written without the r. γujubasu is γuju- 'ask for' + the conditional -basu. The -besü/-basu pair (üžebesü, γujubasu, ögbesü) is vowel harmony. The quotation opens at the first word of the next unit.

morph.gloss: to spend the night (stem inferred) [宿着]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]

sentences.i: "If she is given after many askings, she is held in honour;
sentences.n: A proverb in two halves; this is the first. γujuγ̇ulžu is γuju- + the causative -γ̇ul- + -žu (Ming 索着, which gives only 'asking for'): 'having caused [her] to be asked for', i.e. 'after being asked'. ögbesü is ög- 'give' + the conditional: 'if given'. deġežilegdekü: deġeži 'upper' (Ming 崇上) + -le- (verb) + the passive -gde- + -kü: 'to be raised on high'. The subject, the girl, is not stated. daγ̇u (Ming 遍) counts occasions, 'times'.

morph.gloss: to raise on high (deġeži 'upper'; Ming 崇上) [崇上]

sentences.i: if she is given after few askings, she is looked down on.
sentences.n: The second half, a mirror of the first: čuġen 'few' against olon 'many', doramžilaγdqu against deġežilegdekü. doramžila- is dora 'below' (Ming 下覷, 'look down') + the verbs -mži-/-la-; I give 'to look down on' from the Ming. The passive -γd- + -qu has the back-vowel form here (-qu) against front -kü in the first half.

morph.gloss: to look down on (dora 'below'; Ming 下覷) [下覻]

sentences.t: Ökin küġün-(n)u žajaγ̇an töregsen eġüden -dür ötölkü ügei.
sentences.l: Girl person's fate, born door-at to-grow-old not.
sentences.i: A girl's fate: not to grow old at the door where she was born.
sentences.n: A saying; I make it a generalisation about girls. küġün-(n)u is küġün 'person' + the genitive, so 'a person's fate'; žajaγ̇an 'fate' (Ming 命). töregsen eġüden-dür is 'born door-at'; -dür is written as a separate word (with Ming 裏) and I give it a morph of its own. ötölkü ügei is ötöl- 'grow old' (Ming 老了的) + the participle -kü, then ügei 'not, none' (Ming 無): 'there is no growing old'. The participle phrase töregsen eġüden-dür ('at the door of birth') is the one I find hardest to place; the sense is clear from the Ming word by word.

morph.gloss: to be born; past participle -gsen, 'born, the one born' [生了的]

sentences.t: Ökin(i)-jen be ögsü. Köġün(i)-jen be küriged-te talbižu od" keġebe.
sentences.l: Girl-my-own be give-let. Son-your-own be son-in-law-as put-down, go! said.
sentences.i: I will give my daughter. Leave your son here as son-in-law, and go," he said.
sentences.n: ögsü is ög- 'give' + -sü, the optative of the first person ('let me give', Ming 與). The reflexive -jen points to the subject of its own sentence: 'my' in the first, 'your' in the second (the imperative od 'go!', bare stem, Ming 去, has 'you'). küreged-te: küreged 'son-in-law' (Ming 做女壻, 'to be son-in-law') + -te, which I read as the dative-locative -de written -te after -d, 'as, in the position of'. be (Ming 他, 'he') puzzles me: the form looks like bi 'I' or an emphatic particle, the Ming gloss does not fit, and I leave it unrendered in i. In §§24–42 the same particle after a name was read 'for his part'; the Ming 他 does not support that here, so I do not borrow it. The quotation closes at od.

sentences.i: So, agreeing, Yesügei-Ba'atur said:
sentences.n: že is the particle 'so, very well' (Ming 那般). bolulčažu is bol- 'become' + -lča- 'together' + the converb -žu; Ming 相從, 'follow one another', which I read as 'came to terms'. The stem is my guess. Names: Yesügei-Ba'atur is the full style of Yesügei (Ba'atur 'brave').

morph.gloss: to agree, come to terms (stem inferred; Ming 相從) [相從着]

sentences.i: "I leave my son as son-in-law.
sentences.n: köġü-ben is köġü 'son' + the reflexive -ben 'my own' (-ben/-ban after a vowel; -jen/-jan after a consonant or in the other forms). talbisu is talbi- 'set down' + the optative -su 'let me', the same ending as ögsü.

sentences.i: My son has been afraid of dogs.
sentences.n: noγai-(j)ača is noγai 'dog' + the ablative -(j)ača (Ming 行 'to', the glossator's usual mark for case); the (j) is the glide after a vowel. sočidaγ̇u is a verb for fear (Ming 驚怕), its ending I cannot name; büleġe is the past 'was' of bü-. büleġe and the Ming 有來 are past, so I give 'has been afraid'.

morph.gloss: to be afraid (Ming 驚怕; stem inferred) [驚怕]
to be; past büleġe, 'there was, used to be' [有來]

sentences.t: Quda köġü min-u noγai-(j)ača bu sočiγ̇ul" kēġed
sentences.l: In-law, son my dog-from not frighten, having-said,
sentences.i: In-law, do not let my son be frightened by dogs," he said,
sentences.n: bu is the prohibitive 'do not' (Ming 休), set before the bare stem of a verb: sočiγ̇ul is soči- 'fear' + the causative -γ̇ul-, 'make afraid', so bu sočiγ̇ul = 'do not make [him] afraid'. kēġed is keġe- 'say' + -ġed 'having said' (Ming 說了), the converb that closes a quotation.

sentences.i: giving his own led horse as the betrothal token,
sentences.n: kötöl has Ming 從 'follow, accompany'; I take it as a horse that follows on the lead, but only the Ming is my authority; the stem is kötöl- 'lead' as in kötölžü of the earlier parts, hence 'led horse'. morin(i)-jan is morin 'horse' + the accusative + 'his own'. belge is the 'sign, token' (Ming 定禮, 'betrothal gift'). ögčü is ög- 'give' + -čü 'giving'.

morph.gloss: led, following on the lead (kötöl- 'lead' as in kötölžü; Ming 從; sense uncertain) [從]

sentences.i: he left Temüjin as son-in-law and went away.
sentences.n: Closes the chain that began at že bolulčažu: bolulčažu … ögčü … talbižu … odču. The converbs carry the action and the chain has no finite verb of its own; it runs on into §67 (… odču, žoluγažu, baγ̇ulba). -(n)i is the accusative (Ming 行).

sentences.t: Jesügei-Baγ̇atur žaγ̇ura Čegčer-ün Šira-Keġer-e Tatar irgen qurimlan büküi-dür žoluγažu
sentences.l: Jesügei-Baγ̇atur on-the-road Čegčer's Šira-Keġer-at Tatar people feast-making being-when, meeting,
sentences.i: On the road, as he came upon the Tatar people feasting at Shira-Keger of Chegcher,
sentences.n: büküi-dür is bü- 'be' + the participle -küi + -dür 'at', 'when being': a time-clause, with Tatar irgen (the Tatar people) as its subject, qurimlan (qurim 'feast' + -la- 'make' + -n) as its action (Ming 做筵會 看的時, 'when they were holding a feast'). žoluγažu 'meeting' (Ming 遇着) is the converb of the main action, Yesügei's. žaγ̇ura is žaγ̇ur 'middle' + -a, 'on the way' (Ming 路間). Čegčer-ün Šira-Keġer-e is a place within a place, the genitive then the dative-locative 'at'; both are glossed only 'place name' by the Ming. The chain begun in §66 (… odču) runs into this §.

sentences.i: he was thirsty and dismounted at their feast.
sentences.n: umdasču is a verb for thirst (Ming 渴着) with the converb -ču; the stem umdas- is my inference. an-u is 'their' (Ming 他的), the plural counterpart of in-ü 'his', set after its noun; the Ming gloss makes no difference between them. baγ̇ulba as in §65, 'dismounted'; here the subject is plainly Yesügei.

morph.gloss: their (third-person plural genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]

sentences.i: The Tatars knew him.
sentences.n: Tede 'those, they' (Ming 那的每) is the plural of tere. tanin is tani- 'know, recognise' + -n 'recognising' (Ming 認得), with ažuγ̇u 'was': 'were knowing'. ažuγ̇u is the past of a- 'be' (as in §66).

morph.gloss: to be; past ažuγ̇u, 'there was, he was' [有來]

sentences.i: "Yesügei of the Kiyan has come," they said,
sentences.n: Kijan is the Kiyan, Yesügei's clan (Ming 人氏). ireġei is ire- 'come' + -ġei, a past ending (Ming 了); it is one of a family of past endings that fill the part: -ba, -be, -bi, -ġei, -žuγ̇u, -žüġü, -žüġüi, -čiġüi. I render them all as a plain past and do not claim to say how they differ. The quotation opens at Jesügei and closes at ireġei; the speakers (the Tatars) are not named.

morph.gloss: the Kiyan, a clan (Ming 人氏) [人氏]

sentences.i: remembering their old grudge for those once taken captive, and nursing it in secret,
sentences.n: uridan-u is uridan 'former, earlier' + the genitive (Ming 在前的); daγ̇uliγdaγsan is the passive participle of a verb of capture (Ming 被虜的, 'those taken captive'); together I read 'the grudge for those taken before'. kegesü is 'grudge, vengeance' (Ming 冕讐, a variant of 仇); -ben is the reflexive 'their own', here the Tatars'. duradču 'remembering' (Ming 想着), oisuladun 'secretly harbouring' (Ming 暗懷着); oisula- recurs in §68 as 'secretly harm'. Whose captives is not said; the Tatars' captives taken by Yesügei in §59 seem meant, which is my inference.

morph.gloss: to plunder, take captive (as daγ̇uližu of §§55–63) [被虜︀的]
to act secretly, harbour in secret (Ming 暗懷, 陰害) [暗懷着]

sentences.i: they mixed poison into it and gave it.
sentences.n: qužirču has Ming 毒着 'poisoning', qoro 'poison' (Ming 毒), qoižu 'mixing' (Ming 和着). ögčiġüi is ög- 'give' + a past ending of the -ġüi family (Ming 與了). The object of the giving, the food or drink, is not written. The converb is -ču after r (qužir-ču) but -žu after a vowel (qoi-žu): the choice follows the last sound of the stem: -ču after a consonant, -žu after a vowel.

morph.gloss: to poison (Ming 毒着; stem uncertain) [毒着]

sentences.t: žaγ̇ura maγ̇ui odču γurban qonoγ jabužu
sentences.l: On-the-road ill going, three night travelling,
sentences.i: On the way he went on in poor state, travelling three nights,
sentences.n: maγ̇ui 'bad, evil' (Ming 歹), here of his condition: he is going 'badly'. qonoγ is 'night, halt' (Ming 宿), counted by γurban 'three'. jabužu 'travelling' (Ming 行着). The converbs run on again; the chain closes at bolžu in the next unit.

sentences.i: When he reached his own home he fell ill.
sentences.n: kürüġed is kürü- 'arrive' (the published stem, inferred from the Ming 到) + -ġed 'having arrived' (Ming 到了). maγ̇ui bolžu is 'becoming bad' (Ming 歹做着), 'growing ill'; bol- 'become' is the commonest verb of change, and with an adjective means 'turn …'.

morph.gloss: to arrive (stem inferred from the Ming 到) [到了]

sentences.i: Yesügei-Ba'atur said:
sentences.n: A speech frame: ügülerün 'saying' (Ming 說) is the verb that opens a quotation, here with no finite verb after it.

sentences.i: "I am sick within.
sentences.n: dotora 'inside' (Ming 內), min-u 'my', maγ̇ui 'bad', bi 'is' (Ming 有): no copula supplied in l. Watch bi: it is 'is' here (Ming 有), but twice in the next speech (Bi köġü-ben … and … irgen-e oisulaγdaγa bi) it is 'I' (Ming 我). The Ming distinguishes them; the Mongol letters do not.

sentences.i: Who is near me?" he asked,
sentences.n: dergede 'near, beside' (Ming 根前, 'in front of'): a locative of a stem I cannot identify. ken 'who' (Ming 誰); bi 'is'. keġežü closes the quotation again. A question without a question-particle: ken carries it.

morph.gloss: near, beside (Ming 根前; stem uncertain) [根前]

sentences.t: Qoṅγotadai Čaraqa ebügen-ü köġün Müṅlig oira bi kēġesü
sentences.l: Qoṅγotadai Čaraqa old-man's son Müṅlig near is, saying-when,
sentences.i: "Münlig, son of old Charaqa of the Qongqotadai, is near," they said,
sentences.n: ebügen-ü is ebügen 'old man' + the genitive (Ming 老人的), then köġün 'son': 'old Charaqa's son'. oira 'near' (Ming 根前, the same gloss as dergede). kēġesü is keġe- 'say' + -sü, the conditional-temporal, 'when they said' (Ming 說了); the speakers are not named, so 'they' is my supply. Qoṅγotadai is a people (Ming 種名).

sentences.i: he summoned him, had him come, and said:
sentences.n: urižu 'calling' (Ming 喚着) + ireġülžü 'having made come' (Ming 敎來着): ire- 'come' + the causative -ġül- + -žü. A short chain. ügülerün opens the quotation. I give i as 'summoned … and said' since the subject, Yesügei, is carried on.

sentences.l: Child my Müṅlig, sons small-having were.
sentences.i: "Münlig, my child, the boys were small.
sentences.n: Čaγa (Ming 孩兒 'child') is the address, 'my child Münlig'. üčügetü is üčüge 'small' + the possessive -tü, 'small-having' (Ming 小有的), the front-vowel -tü to the back-vowel -tu: the -tai/-tei/-tu/-tü possessive in all its forms. köġüd is the plural of köġün; whose boys is not said, I take Yesügei's.

morph.gloss: to be; past büleġe, 'there was, used to be' [有來]

sentences.t: Bi köġü-ben Temüžin-i küriged-te talbižu irerün
sentences.l: I son-my-own Temüžin-(acc) son-in-law-as leaving, coming,
sentences.i: "I left my son Temüjin as a son-in-law, and as I was coming back
sentences.n: Bi is 'I' here (Ming 我); contrast bi 'is' in the first speech. talbižu 'leaving'. irerün is ire- 'come' + -rün 'coming, while coming' (Ming 來的). The second half is in the next unit.

morph.gloss: Temüžin (Temüjin), a boy's name [(兒)名 行]

sentences.t: žaγ̇ura Tatar irgen-e oisulaγ- daγ̇a bi.
sentences.i: on the road, I was secretly harmed by the Tatar people.
sentences.n: oisulaγ- and daγ̇a are one verb, split across a line of the printed text (two words, oisulaγ- and daγ̇a): oisula- 'act in secret, harm secretly' (Ming 被陰害了 'was secretly harmed') + the passive -γda- + the past -γ̇a. The agent is in the dative-locative: irgen-e 'by the people' (Ming 行). bi. is 'I' (Ming 我).

morph.gloss: to act secretly, harm in secret [被陰害了]
first part of the passive -γda- (split across the line)

sentences.i: I am sick within."
sentences.n: The refrain of Dotora min-u maγ̇ui bi above, here with bijü, the present of bü-. The two versions stand a few lines apart; they repeat as a formula.

sentences.i: "My little ones, those left behind, my younger brothers,
sentences.n: Three plural nouns in a row: üčüged (üčüge 'small' + the plural -d, as in üčügetü above), qosoluγsad (qosol- 'be left behind' + -γsan + -d, Ming 落後的每) and deġü-ner(i)-jen (deġü 'younger brother' + plural -ner + the accusative + 'my own'). The object is in the accusative; the verb comes in the next unit.

morph.gloss: to be left behind (stem uncertain) [落後的每]

sentences.i: my widow and my sister-in-law: see that you care for them.
sentences.n: belbisün 'widow' (Ming 寡婦). bergen(i)-jen: bergen has Ming 嫂嫂 'sister-in-law', which I keep (the earlier part has berigen, Ming 嫂 'brother's wife'); belbisün and bergen stand side by side with no 'and', so 'widow, sister-in-law' may be one phrase, 'widowed sister-in-law'; whose sister-in-law, and what the 'own' points to, the Ming does not settle. asaraqu-ji is asara- 'tend, care for' (Ming 照覷) + the participle -qu + the accusative, 'the caring for'; či mede is 'you, know!' (Ming 你 知者, the bare imperative mede-), 'mind it'.

morph.gloss: sister-in-law (Ming 嫂嫂; cf. berigen 'brother's wife' in §§43–54) [嫂嫂(自的)行]
to tend, care for [照 覷的 (行)]

sentences.t: Köġü min-u Temüžin-i ötörgen odču abču ire.
sentences.l: Son my Temüžin-(acc) quickly going, taking, come!
sentences.i: Go quickly, fetch my son Temüjin, and bring him back.
sentences.n: A chain ending in the bare imperative ire (Ming 來): odču 'going', abču 'taking', ire 'come!'. ötörgen 'quickly' (Ming 快); ötör in §69 is the same word without -gen.

morph.gloss: Temüžin (Temüjin), a boy's name [(兒)名 行]

sentences.i: Münlig, my child," he said, and died.
sentences.n: The address closes the quotation: čaγa min-u Müṅlig. Then kēġed 'having said' and the finite nögčibe (Ming 死了, 'died'), where nögči- is a stem I infer, a plain way of saying that Yesügei died. Compare üküleġü 'is dead' (§70).

morph.gloss: to die (Ming 死了; stem inferred) [死了]

sentences.t: Jesügei-Baγ̇atur-un üge-ji buši ülü bolγan Müṅlig odču De-Sečen-(n)e ügülerün:
sentences.l: Jesügei-Baγ̇atur's word-(acc) otherwise not making, Müṅlig going, to-De-Sečen saying:
sentences.i: Not setting aside Yesügei-Ba'atur's word, Münlig went to De-Sechen and said:
sentences.n: bolγan is bol- 'become' + the causative -γa- + the converb -n (Ming 做了), 'making', as in the published bolγan; buši ülü bolγan, 'not making [it] otherwise' (buši, Ming 別, 'other'), so 'not departing from his word'. üge-ji is üge 'word' (Ming 言語) + the accusative. -(n)e is the dative-locative 'to' (Ming 行). This is a long sentence, a chain of three converbs ending in ügülerün; I leave it unbroken.

morph.gloss: Jesügei-Baγ̇atur (Yesügei-Ba'atur), a man's name [人名 勇士 的]
De-Sečen (De-Sechen), a man's name [人名 行]

sentences.t: "Jesügei aqa Temüžin-i maši mörelžü öre-ben ebedümü.
sentences.l: Jesügei elder-brother Temüžin-(acc) greatly thinking-of, heart-his-own aching.
sentences.i: "Elder brother Yesügei thinks greatly of Temüjin, and his heart aches.
sentences.n: aqa 'elder brother' (Ming 兄) is an honorific, 'brother Yesügei'. maši 'much, greatly' (Ming 好生). mörelžü 'thinking of' (Ming 思想着): the stem mörel- is inferred. öre-ben, 'his own heart' (Ming 心), is öre (my reading of the stem) + the reflexive. ebedümü is ebed- 'be sick, hurt' (Ming 疼) + the present -ümü; compare saγ̇ulumu (§64) for vowel harmony in the ending.

morph.gloss: Temüžin (Temüjin), a boy's name [(兒)名 行]
to think of, long for (stem inferred) [思想着]
heart (Ming 心; stem uncertain) [心 自的行]

sentences.i: I have come to fetch Temüjin," he said.
sentences.n: abura is ab- 'take' + a purposive converb (-ura, the back-vowel partner of the -re of üžere in §73; Ming 取), 'in order to take'. irebe 'came'. keġežüġü, 'he said' (Ming 說有), is keġe- + -žüġü, the narrative past; that ending in all its harmony forms, -žuγ̇u/-žüġü/-žüġüi, closes quotations throughout the part.

morph.gloss: Temüžin (Temüjin), a boy's name [(兒名) 行]
converb of purpose: in order to

sentences.i: De-Sechen said:
sentences.n: The speech frame again. De-Sečen's answer is in the next two units.

sentences.i: "If the in-law is thinking of his son, let [the boy] go;
sentences.n: mörelkü is mörel- (see mörelžü in the first speech of this §) + the participle -kü; böġesü is bü- 'be' in the conditional (Ming 有呵), 'if it be that'. odtuγai is od- 'go' + -tuγai, the optative (Ming 敎去, 'let go'): the back-vowel partner of -tügei (üžetügei, iretügei). Shiratori's semicolon after odtuγai marks the end of the first half. The one to go is not named: the son, Temüjin.

morph.gloss: to think of, long for (stem inferred) [思想]
to be; conditional böġesü, 'if it be, if it is that' [有呵]

sentences.i: and when he has seen him, let him come quickly back," he said,
sentences.n: The second half: üžežü 'seeing', ötör 'quickly', iretügei 'let him come' (ire- + the optative -tügei, the front-vowel form). keġežü ends the quotation and begins the narrative.

sentences.i: Father Münlig took Temüjin and came.
sentences.n: Müṅlig ečige is 'father Münlig' (Ming 人名 父), ečige 'father' as a respectful title for an older man, as aqa is for Yesügei. I read it as the same Münlig, not a different person; the Ming does not say whether the two are one man.

morph.gloss: Temüžin (Temüjin), a boy's name [(兒)名 行]

sentences.t: Tere qabur Ambaγai qaγan-(n)u qatud Orba, Soqatai žirin jekes-e γažar-u inerü γaruγsan-dur
sentences.l: That spring Ambaγai Qaγan's queens Orba, Soqatai two, elders-to place-of offering going-out-when,
sentences.i: That spring, when Ambaqai Qahan's two queens, Orba and Soqatai, went out to the elders' ground for the offering,
sentences.n: A time-clause ending in -γsan-dur: γar- 'go out' + the participle -γsan + -dur 'when' (Ming 出去了時). qatud is the plural of qatun 'queen'; Orba, Soqatai žirin is the pair 'Orba and Soqatai, two' (Ming 兩箇). The last four words I read with doubt: jekes-e is jeke 'great' + -s + the dative-locative -e (Ming 大的每行, 'to the great ones, the elders'), γažar-u 'of the place' (Ming 地裏), inerü a rite of burnt offering of food (Ming 燒飯祭祀; the word itself I cannot analyse). A dative-locative and a genitive stand side by side and I cannot say which depends on which; the sense 'for the offering at the elders' ground' is a reading of the Ming.

morph.gloss: burnt offering of food (Ming 燒飯祭祀; word uncertain) [燒飯︀祭祀]
to go out [出去了 時]

sentences.i: Högelün-Üjin went, arrived late, and was left behind,
sentences.n: Chain of converbs: odču 'going', kürčü 'arriving', qožidaγ̇uldažu (Ming 被落後了着, 'having been made to lag'). qožid 'behind, late' (Ming 落後) stands before kürčü as an adverb; the verb is built on the same word, qožid- + the causative -γ̇ul- + a further -da- (perhaps passive) + -žu, and I cannot split it with confidence. The meaning is that she was not served with the rest.

morph.gloss: to lag, be late (Ming 落後) [被落後了着]

sentences.i: Högelün-Üjin said to the two, Orba and Soqatai:
sentences.n: Högelün is the speaker (the next unit's words are hers). žirin-e is žirin 'two' + the dative-locative -e, 'to the two' (Ming 兩箇行).

sentences.i: "Saying that Yesügei-Ba'atur is dead,
sentences.n: keġežü is 'saying' (Ming 說着): the words 'Yesügei is dead' are quoted as what they say, and the clause after it (my sons are not yet grown) carries the reason; I keep 'saying'. üküleġü is üküle- 'die' (Ming 死了) with an ending I cannot name, 'is dead'. The accusative -i on Yesügei is odd with 'dead'; I note it and read the clause as 'Yesügei being dead'.

morph.gloss: Jesügei-Baγ̇atur (Yesügei-Ba'atur), a man's name [人名 勇士 行]

sentences.i: since my sons are not yet grown,
sentences.n: boluqui-(j)ača is bol- + the participle -qui + the ablative -(j)ača, 'from the becoming', 'since they are not becoming' (Ming 做的行). ülü negates the participle. jeke 'big' (Ming 大) is the adjective: 'not becoming big' = 'not yet grown'.

sentences.t: jekes-ün kešig-eče bileġür-eče sarqu-dača jakin qožidaγ̇ulumui ta
sentences.l: Elders'-of share-from, remainder-from, sacrificial-meat-from, why leave-behind-do you?
sentences.i: why do you leave us out of the elders' share, of the leavings, of the offered meat?
sentences.n: Three ablatives in a row: kešig-eče 'from the share' (Ming 分子), bileġür-eče 'from the remainder' (Ming 餘胙), sarqu-dača 'from the sacrificial meat' (Ming 胙). The ablative is -eče after front vowels, -ača after back ones, and -dača after the -u of sarqu; the Ming glosses two of them with 內 or 行 and leaves the middle one bare. jakin 'why, how' (Ming 如何). qožidaγ̇ulumui is the verb of qožidaγ̇uldažu (above) in a finite present (-umui, Ming 有), with ta 'you' set after it as in ba and či.

morph.gloss: remainder of an offering (Ming 餘胙; word uncertain) [餘胙]
to lag, be left behind [敎落後了有]

sentences.t: üžeġed ideküi ülü sergüġülün neġükün boluba ta" keġežüġü.
sentences.l: Seeing, eating not rousing, moving-off became, you, saying-was.
sentences.i: Seeing it, you broke camp without rousing us to eat," she said.
sentences.n: üžeġed is üže- + -ġed, 'having seen'; ideküi is ide- 'eat' + the participle -küi (Ming 喫); ülü sergüġülün is 'not rousing' (sergüġül- 'wake', Ming 呼醒, + the converb -n), under ülü. neġükün boluba: neġü- 'move off, break camp' (Ming 起) + -kün + bol- + -ba, 'came to move'; I read -kün as a participle-like ending, and the whole as 'moved off'. ta 'you' (Ming 您) is the subject again at the end, then keġežüġü 'said'.

morph.gloss: to rouse, wake (Ming 呼醒) [呼醒]

sentences.t: Tere üge-dür Orba, Soqatai žirin qatud ügülerün:
sentences.l: That word-at Orba, Soqatai two queens saying:
sentences.i: At those words the two queens, Orba and Soqatai, said:
sentences.n: tere üge-dür 'at that word' (Ming 那 言語裏): dative-locative as 'at, upon'. The speech that follows I find the hardest in the part; where I am unsure it is in the notes below.

sentences.t: "Urižu ülü ögteküi mörtei či učiraγ̇asu idekü josutai či;
sentences.l: Calling, not to-be-given way-having you; meeting-if, eating right-having you;
sentences.i: "When called, it is your way not to be given; if you chance upon it, it is right that you eat;
sentences.n: Two clauses set against each other, 'called' against 'chance upon'. ögteküi: ög- 'give' + -te- (a passive or potential element, Ming 可與的 'fit to be given') + the participle -küi; mörtei is mör 'way, custom' (Ming 道子) + the possessive -tei, 'way-having'; josutai is josun 'rule, right' (Ming 理) + -tai, 'right-having'. So 'for you it is the way not to be given; for you it is right to eat': another possessive pair. učiraγ̇asu is učira- 'meet' + the conditional -γ̇asu (the back-vowel partner of -besü). I give the sense with real doubt; the Ming for each word is clear, the force of the whole is not.

sentences.t: kürežü ülü ögtekü mörtei či; kürteġesü idekü josutai či;
sentences.l: Inviting not to-be-given way-having you; arrive-if, eating right-having you;
sentences.i: if you are invited, it is your way not to be given; if you arrive, it is right that you eat;
sentences.n: The same pair with kürežü 'inviting' (Ming 請着) and kürteġesü 'if arrive' (kür- + a conditional, Ming 若到呵). Shiratori punctuates with semicolons after each či; I follow him. ögtekü here has the participle -kü (the first was -küi), both Ming 可與的; the difference I do not claim to explain.

morph.gloss: to invite (Ming 請着; stem uncertain) [請着]

sentences.i: Ambaqai Qahan is dead, and you —"
sentences.n: I give the clause as it stands: Ambaγai qaγan-(n)i (Ming 皇帝行, accusative) üküleġü (Ming 死了, 'dead') and či 'you'. The accusative with 'dead' would suit a sense like 'you [brought on] the death', but the Ming says only 'dead'; I leave it open. The closing mark follows či. The same formula, a name in the accusative before üküleġü, stands in Högelün's own speech above (Yesügei-Baγ̇atur-i üküleġü keġežü), so this may be the queens' quotation of her complaint; I do not press it.

sentences.t: keġežü Höġelün-(n)e kürtele ein keġegdeküi bolbi.
sentences.l: Saying, Högelün-to until, thus being-said became.
sentences.i: So they spoke, and so it was said even to Högelün.
sentences.n: keġegdeküi is keġe- 'say' + the passive -gde- + -küi, 'being said' (Ming 被說). kürtele is kür- 'reach' + -tele 'until' (Ming 到了): 'up to Högelün'. ein 'thus, so' (Ming 這般). bolbi is bol- + -bi, 'became' (Ming 做了); -bi is another past ending beside -ba/-be. Reading: 'such words were said, to the extent of reaching Högelün'.

morph.gloss: Höġelün (Högelün), a woman's name [太祖︀母名 行]

sentences.t: Araγača eden-i ekes köġüd-i nutuγ-tur gežü neġüdkün; ta ber bu abču jabudqun" kēġed
sentences.l: As-for, these-(acc) mothers, sons-(acc) camp-in leaving, move-you-all; you also not taking go-you-all, having-said,
sentences.i: "As for these, the mothers and sons, leave them in the camp and move off, all of you; and do not take them with you either," they said,
sentences.n: Imperatives. Plural: neġüdkün and jabudqun end in -kün/-qun after an unexplained -d- (as in kesedkün of §§43–54), the plural imperative 'you all …!' (Ming 您 added to each). abču 'taking' (Ming 將着), bu 'do not' (Ming 休). gežü has Ming 撇着 'casting off, leaving'; the stem ge- I do not know. Araγača has Ming 論來, 'as for, speaking of'; the form I cannot analyse. ekes is the plural of eke 'mother' (Ming 母(每)); with köġüd-i 'sons' it names the group left behind. ber: 'also' (Ming 也). The speakers (the queens) are not named here.

morph.gloss: as for, speaking of (Ming 論來; form unclear) [論來]
to leave, cast off (stem uncertain) [撇着]
element of unknown force, uncertain (as in kesedkün, soridqun of §§43–54)
element of unknown force, uncertain (as in kesedkün, soridqun of §§43–54)

sentences.t: manaγar-ši üdür-eče Taičiγ̇ud-un Tarγutai-Kiriltuγ, Tödöġen-Girte-ten Taičiγ̇ud Onan müren huruγ̇u ködölbe.
sentences.l: Tomorrow-toward day-from, Taičiγ̇ud's Tarγutai-Kiriltuγ, Tödöġen-Girte-and-the-like, Taičiγ̇ud, Onan river downstream moved.
sentences.i: From the next day Tarqutai-Kiriltuq of the Taichi'ud, Tödögen-Girte and the rest, the Taichi'ud, moved off down the river Onan.
sentences.n: manaγar-ši üdür-eče (Ming 明日 日自) 'from the day toward tomorrow', 'from the next day'. Taičiγ̇ud-un is the genitive 'of the Taichi'ud', followed by the leaders' names; -ten on Girte-ten is the plural 'and the like' (Ming 等). Onan müren is the river name and its common noun; huruγ̇u 'downstream, along' (Ming 順). ködölbe is ködöl- 'move' + -be (Ming 動了). Note Taičiγ̇ud twice, in the genitive and in the nominative that is the subject.

sentences.i: leaving Högelün-Üjin, the mothers and the sons, behind as they moved off,
sentences.n: The Taichi'ud's act seen from the other side: gežü 'leaving' (Ming 撇着) governs the accusative objects, and neġügderün 'as they moved off' (neġü- 'move' + -gde- + the converb -rün, Ming 起了) is the time of it. I read -gde- here as a passive or plural mark and do not press it. ekes köġüd-i 'mothers, sons' repeats the queens' words above.

morph.gloss: Höġelün-Üžin (Högelün-Üjin), a woman's name [太祖︀母名 行]
to leave, cast off (stem uncertain) [撇着]

sentences.i: when old Charaqa of the Qongqotadai went and urged them,
sentences.n: idqaqu-dur is idqa- 'urge' (Ming 勸) + the participle -qu + -dur 'when'. I give 'urge' on the Ming alone; the stem is not known to me and the sense of the urging (to stay, to turn back?) is not in the words. Čaraγa ebügen: a name followed by the title 'old man', as before.

morph.gloss: to urge, exhort (Ming 勸; stem uncertain) [勸時]

sentences.t: Tödöġen-Girte ügülerün; "Čeġel usun niduraluγ̇a. Čegen čilaγ̇un čaγ̇uraluγ̇a" keġeġed neġüžeġei.
sentences.l: Tödöġen-Girte saying: "Deep water has dried. Bright stone has crumbled," saying, moved-off.
sentences.i: Tödögen-Girte said: "The deep water has run dry; the bright stone has crumbled." So saying, they moved off.
sentences.n: Two short finite sentences in the past -luγ̇a (nidura-luγ̇a, čaγ̇ura-luγ̇a, Ming 了); the stems nidura- 'dry up' (Ming 乾) and čaγ̇ura- 'crumble, break' (Ming 碎) are inferred from the Ming. čeġel has Ming 深 'deep', čegen Ming 明 'bright'. The pair reads as a figure, but the Ming does not say of what, and I do not press it. keġeġed neġüžeġei closes it: neġü- + -žeġei, the same past as -žüġüi in neġüžüġüi (§73), spelled with e for ü; I do not claim to say why.

sentences.t: Čaraγa ebügen-i ker idqaqu či keġen
sentences.l: Čaraγa old-man-(acc): how urge you, saying,
sentences.i: "How is it that you urge?" they said to old Charaqa,
sentences.n: A speech in two parts, 'how do you urge?' (ker idqaqu či; ker Ming 怎生 'how'), then keġen 'saying' (Ming 麽道). ebügen-i is accusative: Charaqa is the object of the stab that follows in the next unit, so the accusative is given as 'said to' him. The speakers (Tödögen-Girte and his men) are not named.

sentences.i: and they thrust a spear into him from behind, along the spine.
sentences.n: qoināča 'from behind' (qoina + the ablative -ča). žida-bar: žida 'spear' (Ming 槍) + -bar, the instrumental 'with' (Ming gives no case-word). čoγudus has Ming 脊肉順, 'along the spine-flesh': the word I cannot analyse. qadqužuγ̇u is qadqu- 'thrust, stab' (Ming 刺) + -žuγ̇u, the past narrative; this -žuγ̇u/-žüġü/-žüġüi/-ġei family is flagged at ireġei in §67.

morph.gloss: along the spine (Ming 脊肉順; word uncertain) [脊肉順]

sentences.t: Čaraγa ebügen jaratu bolžu ger-tür(i)-jen irežü berke kebteküi-dür Temüžin üžere odčuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Čaraγa old-man wound-having becoming, own-home-to coming, hard lying-when, Temüžin to-see went.
sentences.i: Old Charaqa, wounded, came to his home, and as he lay in a bad way, Temüjin went to see him.
sentences.n: A time-clause: kebteküi-dür is kebte- 'lie down' (Ming 臥) + -küi + -dür, 'when lying'; berke 'hard, severe' (Ming 艱難) says how. jaratu is jara 'wound' + the possessive -tu, 'wound-having' (Ming 傷有的), and bolžu 'becoming'. The subject changes at Temüžin: the lying man is Charaqa, the one who goes is Temüjin. üžere is the purposive converb 'to see' (as in the earlier parts), and odčuγ̇u the narrative past 'went'.

sentences.i: There old Charaqa of the Qongqotadai said:
sentences.n: tende 'there, then' (Ming 那裏). ügülerün opens the quotation, which runs to kigdebe at the end of the speech.

sentences.t: "Sain ečige-jin čin-u qurijaγdaγsan ulus-i man-u bürin-ü ulus abču neġügderün
sentences.l: Good father-of your gathered people-(acc), our all-of people, taking, as-they-moved-off,
sentences.i: "The people your good father gathered, all our people, they took with them as they moved off;
sentences.n: A noun phrase, then a converb. ečige-jin čin-u 'your father's' (Ming 父的 你的); sain 'good' (Ming 好) before it; qurijaγdaγsan, 'gathered' (Ming 收來的), a passive participle of qurija- (stem inferred: qurija-γda-γsan); ulus-i, the object, and man-u bürin-ü ulus ('our all-of people', Ming 衆的), a second wording of the same people. abču neġügderün 'taking, as they moved off': the Taichi'ud are the subject but not named. The possessor man-u comes before its noun here, not after it.

morph.gloss: to gather (stem inferred; the word reads qurija-γda-γsan) [收來的]

sentences.i: when I urged them, this was done to me," he said.
sentences.n: idqaqu bolun, 'at the time of urging' (bol- + -un, Ming 時). kigdebe is ki- 'do' + the passive -gde- + -be, 'was done' (Ming 做了); ein kigdebe 'thus was done', with the doer left out, as in the English. kēžügü 'he said' (Ming 說了) closes the quotation: another form of the narrative past.

sentences.i: Then Temüjin wept, went out, and set off.
sentences.n: Teġün-dür is the oblique stem teġün- of tere 'that' + -dür (Ming 那的 裏): 'thereupon'. uilaγ̇ad is uila- 'weep' (Ming 哭) + the converb -γ̇ad; γarču 'going out' (γar- + -ču); jorčiba, as in the earlier parts, 'set out' (Ming 去了).

morph.gloss: that (oblique stem of tere) [那的 裏]
to set out, go (Ming 去; stem inferred) [去了]

sentences.i: Högelün-Üjin, left behind as they moved off,
sentences.n: Höġelün-Üžin has no accusative here, so she is the subject of the verbs of the next unit (the banner, the horse, the turning back): 'Högelün, left (by them) as they moved off', as in the unit where the Taichi'ud leave her, only without the accusative. gežü and neġügderün are as in the unit where the Taichi'ud leave Högelün.

morph.gloss: to leave, cast off (stem uncertain) [撇着]

sentences.t: tuγlažu beje-ber morilažu žarimud irgen-i ičuγaba.
sentences.l: Banner taking, herself horse-mounting, half people-(acc) turned-back.
sentences.i: took up the banner, mounted her horse herself, and turned half the people back.
sentences.n: tuγlažu has Ming (英)頭拿着, 'taking up the head [of the standard]': tuγ 'banner' + -la- (verb-making) + -žu; stem inferred. beje-ber is beje 'body' + -ber, 'in person, herself' (Ming 親身). morilažu is morin 'horse' + -la- 'to mount' (Ming 上馬着). žarimud irgen-i, 'half the people' (Ming 一半), is accusative as the object of ičuγaba 'turned back' (Ming 退了). A chain of two converbs and one finite verb.

morph.gloss: to turn back, drive back (Ming 退) [退了]

sentences.t: Tede ber ičuγaγdaγsan irgen ülü toγtan
sentences.l: Those also turned-back people not settling,
sentences.i: Even those people, turned back, did not settle,
sentences.n: Tede ber, 'those also' (Ming 那的每 也). ičuγaγdaγsan is the passive participle of ičuγa-: 'the turned-back'. toγtan is toγta- 'settle' (Ming 定) + the converb -n, with ülü 'not' before it: 'not settling'. The sentence ends in the next unit.

sentences.i: but moved off after the Taichi'ud.
sentences.n: qoināča 'from behind' (as in the spearing unit), here with the genitive Taičiγ̇ud-un, 'from behind the Taichi'ud': I read 'after them', trailing them. neġüžüġüi is neġü- + -žüġüi, the narrative past; its sibling is the earlier neġüžeġei.
